diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and Verification 2.1 define X:(0,1)^2 -> R^3 by X(y1,y2)=(y1,y2,2y1-y2+3). Diagram square and graph are closure outlines only, with excluded edges declared in the caption. Vertex images are (0,0,3),(1,0,5),(1,1,4),(0,1,2).

Using translated parallel projection P(x,y,z)=(x+0.65y,-0.25x+0.4y+0.65(z-3)), the four images are (0,0),(1,1.05),(1.65,0.8),(0.65,-0.25), exactly the drawn patch. From Verification 1.1/2.1, t1=(1,0,2), t2=(0,1,-1); their projected directions are (1,1.05), (0.65,-0.25). Each displayed tangent arrow displacement is 0.66 of that direction.

t1 cross t2=(-2,1,1)=N; t1 dot N=-2+2=0 and t2 dot N=1-1=0. For z-h(y), derivative along N is 1+|Dh|^2=6>0, so N points out of the subgraph, exactly as Verification 1.1 states. P(N)=(-1.35,1.55); normal arrow displacement (-0.81,0.93)=0.6P(N), preserving outward orientation. No projected right-angle assertion is made.

Verification 2.1 has |N|=sqrt(6), hence dS=sqrt(6)dy1dy2, and e3 dot N=1. Parameter square has area 1, giving surface area sqrt(6) and upward flux 1. Figure label and accompanying text repeat precisely these computations.

Both outlines use four explicit closing segments. Actual compiled SVG has four square edges and four parallelogram edges, each vertex degree two; the patch SVG relative displacements sum to zero. No open/closed endpoint rings are used; excluded boundary is conveyed by dashed lines plus explicit prose. Original Verification is byte-identical and independent of the illustration.
